source_title: Pathways to the emergency department - a national, cross-sectional study in Sweden
locator: Abstract; Results, pathway to ED and admission by pathway.
source_setting: Adult arrivals at 43 of Sweden’s 72 emergency departments; all patients present over an observed 24-hour period.
source_n: 3,875 adults overall; complete pathway data n=3,693; triage acuity recorded for n=3,365.
quantity: Observed pathway composition and admission share by arrival pathway
unit: patients; percent of pathway-complete sample or pathway subgroup
source_evidence_basis: National cross-sectional direct observation across 43 EDs: self-referred walk-in was the commonest pathway, followed by ambulance; ambulance arrivals had the highest admission rate.
limitations: One day, Sweden; nonrandom pathway groups differ in age and acuity. Does not specify registration or handoff durations, and admission proportions are not local arrival probabilities.
inferred_scenario_use: Represent arrival mode as an explicit branch into front-door workflows, with ambulance arrivals carrying a different acuity/admission mix only as an external scenario reference; do not assign RWJ rates from this study.

source_title: A Novel Approach to Addressing an Unintended Consequence of Direct to Room: The Delay of Initial Vital Signs
locator: Abstract and Methods/Results; TTVS defined as quick registration to first documented vital sign.
source_setting: Single academic tertiary ED, Staten Island University Hospital, New York; ambulatory entry via quick registration and direct-to-room or formal triage pathways.
source_period: Control 2014-11-01 to 2015-05-01; intervention 2015-11-01 to 2016-05-01; included 07:00-23:00 arrivals.
quantity: Mean time from quick registration to first documented vital sign
source_evidence_basis: Retrospective before-after cohort reports means and Ns; intervention placed a patient-care assistant at a waiting-area vital-sign station coupled to quick registration.
limitations: Single-center nonrandomized before/after implementation and restricted hours; pre/post cohort dates are a year apart. Does not quantify identity verification failure, completion of full triage, or effects in EMS arrivals. Source reports35% reduction; rounded endpoint means15.3 and9.8 imply about35.95%. Preserve reported value rather than treat it as a recomputed rate.
inferred_scenario_use: Model quick demographic/chief-complaint registration, initial vital signs, and formal nurse triage as distinct events; use the pre/post timing only as an external workflow scenario, never as RWJ timing.

source_title: The effect of emergency department crowding on reassessment of children with critically abnormal vital signs
locator: Abstract, Methods and Results; triage vital-sign reassessment, electronic alert after 1 hour.
source_setting: Pediatric ED at Cincinnati Children’s Hospital Medical Center; patients placed in regular ED rooms after critically abnormal triage vital signs.
source_n: 9,976 patients with critically abnormal triage vital signs among 253,408 visits (3.9%).
quantity: Mean time to repeat vital signs and association between crowding and reassessment rate
unit: minutes; relative reassessment rate per 10 patients
source_evidence_basis: Retrospective cross-sectional cohort, Cox time-to-event analysis; electronic alerts prompted reassessment after one hour. Crowding correlated with slower reassessment.
limitations: Pediatric single-center retrospective study; sample restricted to patients with critically abnormal triage vitals placed in regular rooms, not all waiting-room arrivals. Association does not establish causation or a staffing standard.
inferred_scenario_use: Represent waiting after triage as an active monitored state with a reassessment due event and escalation pathway; test missed/delayed reassessment under congestion without borrowing a RWJ interval or probability.

source_title: Factors Associated with Patients Leaving Without Being Seen in a Canadian Emergency Department
locator: Abstract; Results; Table, LWBS denominator and adjusted operational factors.
source_setting: The Ottawa Hospital General Campus, tertiary-care/cancer-center ED, Canada.
source_n: 170,536 ED encounters; 15,473 LWBS; 2,716 left before triage.
quantity: LWBS and pre-triage departure shares; adjusted odds change with queue counts
unit: encounters; percent; adjusted odds ratio per five people
source_evidence_basis: All-encounter retrospective cohort; the paper reports 9.1% in abstract and 9.2% in detailed results (15,473/170,536 is about 9.1%). Pre-triage departures were separately counted. Adjusted odds rose with both waiting-patient and awaiting-disposition counts.
limitations: Single Canadian center, observational design; records did not include arrival method and authors did not report downstream outcomes for departures. Percent rounding differs between abstract and detailed text.
inferred_scenario_use: Keep registered-but-not-triaged departure and post-triage/pre-physician LWBS as separate absorbing outcomes, linked to queue state. Treat reported associations as external evidence, not transferable departure probabilities.

source_title: Guidance for emergency departments: initial assessment
source_setting: NHS England emergency department guidance, England.
source_n: Not applicable; operational guidance, not a cohort.
quantity: Target process for non-pre-alerted ambulance handover
value: Complete handover following locally agreed processes within 15 minutes of arrival; pre-alerted patients needing a clinical team should be received immediately; hospital responsibility for clinical assessment/treatment begins when ambulance arrives at department.
unit: minutes from ED arrival; workflow requirement
source_evidence_basis: Official NHS England guidance distinguishes heralded ambulance patients from unheralded self-presenters, sets separate handover process expectations, and states responsibility transfer at arrival.
limitations: England operational guidance, not an observed compliance estimate; local pathways and regulatory context may differ. Does not define a US hospital’s identity/registration steps.
inferred_scenario_use: Model ambulance arrival, pre-alert, immediate clinical receipt versus standard handover, then destination; keep administrative registration from delaying clinical ownership. Use 15 minutes as policy reference only, not actual RWJ handover time.

source_title: Protocol for the handover of ambulance patients in the Emergency Department process map
locator: Process map: clinical handover process, triage, registration, ED treatment location and data capture points.
source_setting: Victorian Department of Health ambulance-to-ED handover process guidance.
source_n: Not applicable; official process map, not a cohort.
value: After arrival and clinical handover, ED location is immediately available as treatment space or waiting room depending on patient condition and acuity; if no ED location is available, patient remains on ambulance stretcher with regular triage-nurse review. Process map separately records triage and registration.
source_evidence_basis: Inspected the original one-page PDF: it explicitly shows pre-arrival review, IMIST-AMBO handover, triage and registration, transfer to a treatment space/chair/waiting room when location is available, or ambulance-stretcher hold with regular triage-nurse review plus escalation arrangements when no location is available within local thresholds. It defines the handover-complete timestamp after agreement, clinician acceptance of responsibility and related tasks.
limitations: A stated process design, not measured compliance, frequency, or elapsed-time distribution; Australian workflow may not match RWJ.
inferred_scenario_use: Add distinct EMS stretcher-hold, repeat nurse review, registration, and placement transitions. Do not infer how often the hold occurs or its duration.

source_title: Surveillance of Patients in the Waiting Area of the Department of Emergency Medicine
locator: Abstract; Methods and Results, waiting-area wireless vital sign monitoring.
source_setting: Single high-volume German emergency department; selected patients with acute cardiac/pulmonary symptoms or potentially life-threatening conditions.
source_period: Study period not specified in the inspected abstract/text excerpt.
source_n: 230 enrolled patients; 4 terminated participation early; 684 monitoring hours.
quantity: Duration of waiting-area vital-sign observation in feasibility cohort
unit: minutes per patient (median, IQR); total monitored hours
source_evidence_basis: Single-center observational cross-sectional feasibility study reports enrollment, monitoring time, aggregate monitored hours, and use of continuous wireless vital-sign data to assist care.
limitations: Selected higher-risk consenting patients, small feasibility cohort, no control group and no estimate of deterioration incidence or outcome benefit; source period unavailable from excerpt.
inferred_scenario_use: Treat waiting-room monitoring and detection/escalation as a possible staffed capability for a high-risk subgroup, not a default universal workflow or a probability model.
